**Key insight from round 2:**
The champion (-3.07) is a simple 2-state machine:
- S0: GoToColor(blue/6) → go to blue source (decreases score = GOOD!)
  - On white floor (nest): transition with p=0.9 → back to S0
  - On black floor (source): transition with p=0.3 → go to S1
- S1: GoToColor(red/1) → go to nest wall
  - On white floor: transition with p=0.05 (rarely leave)

Wait, let me re-read: S0 goes toward blue (clr=6), transitions on WHITE (C=2, p=0.9→S0 self... no, destination 0 means "other state" = S1) and BLACK (C=0, p=0.3→S1). S1 goes toward red/nest (clr=1), transitions on WHITE (p=0.05→S0) and BLACK (p=0.9→S0).

So the logic is: **Go to blue source** → when on black (source area), sometimes switch to **Go to red/nest** → when on black again (shouldn't happen much), go back; when on white (nest), rarely switch back.

This makes sense! Blue walls are behind the GOOD half (decreases score). The robot picks up blue items and delivers them to the nest.

The green-source machine scored -0.34 (rank 6 in round 1) but the blue-source machine scored -3.07. So BLUE is the good half.

1. Keep champion (elitism)
2. Exploit champion: tweak p values (0.9, 0.3, 0.05, 0.9)

4. Try adding gray floor detection

The transitions in S0: on white (nest) go to S1 (nest-goer), on black (source) sometimes go to S1. This means when robot arrives at source (black), it has 30% chance to switch to going-to-nest. That seems right for delivery.
